title: Prove D(5)=12 from Scratch
problemStatement: Prove from scratch (no new axioms) that the minimal diameter of an admissible 5-tuple is exactly 12: minAdmissibleDiameter 5 = 12. Witness {0,2,6,8,12} (diameter 12, admissible); lower bound D(5) >= 12 is the k=5 entry of OEIS A008407 and is a finite, decidable check.
knownResults: Parent BoundedPrimeGapsOQ03OQ01.lean proves minAdmissibleDiameter_2 = 2 and minAdmissibleDiameter_3 = 6 from scratch.
D(50)=246 is an axiom (Engelsma 2013). D(5)=12 is OEIS A008407(5).
references: OEIS A008407 (minimal diameter of admissible k-tuple)
Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Ann. of Math. 2015

insights: This slug had NO materialized statement in the registry; interpreted as the D(5)=12 rung by analogy to proved D(2)/D(3) and the D(4)=8 sibling.
D(5)=12 is finite/decidable (OEIS A008407), distinct from the parent's open '246 barrier' — buildable, just build-gated this session.

Lower bound D(5)>=12 reduces to: shift to min=0 (translation-invariance of IsAdmissible) + native_decide over the 5-subsets of {0,...,11}, each inadmissible mod 2 or mod 3 (only p in {2,3,5} can cover a 5-set of width <=11; p=2,3 suffice).
Witness {0,2,6,8,12}: admissible since mod 2 -> {0}, mod 3 -> {0,2}, mod 5 -> {0,1,2,3}, each missing a class; p>=7 cannot cover 5 points.

MERGED lower bound is native_decide-FREE: p=2 admissibility forces all elements to share min's parity; diameter<12 then confines H to the 6-set {m,m+2,m+4,m+6,m+8,m+10}; its two disjoint mod-3-complete triples {m,m+2,m+4} and {m+6,m+8,m+10} each must omit >=1 element (else H covers all residues mod 3), forcing >=2 omissions from a 6-set — impossible for card 5. Only primes p in {2,3} are interrogated, so no Decidable IsAdmissible instance is needed.

The merged proof is strictly cleaner than the S1 draft plan (which anticipated native_decide over the 5-subsets of {0..11}): the symbolic parity + mod-3-triple-covering argument needs no closed-term reduction, so the headline carries no Lean.ofReduceBool axiom.

De Polignac bracket floor(2n/d) - 2 floor(n/d) in {0,1}: the <=1 direction reduces (via Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul + Nat.lt_succ_iff) to 2n < (2 floor(n/d) + 2) d, closed by nlinarith on Nat.div_add_mod + Nat.mod_lt (nonlinear in d, n/d — omega cannot, nlinarith can).

L2 only needs L1 at N=2n and N=n; the N=n sum extends from Ioc 0 n to Ioc 0 2n via Finset.sum_subset since n/d=0 for d>n (Nat.div_eq_of_lt). psi(2n) unfolds via Chebyshev.psi with floor(2*n)=2n (Nat.floor_natCast). Remaining open piece: assembly chebyshev_psi_lower_bound (real-analysis, c=(log4)/4, log(2n)=o(n)).
